messages.author: b0eff9b40a74c4a8
messages.subject: Color internal branches error.
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to color the branches of the tree with specific colors.
However, when I add color according to their Phylum, the internal branches disappear.
Any idea on how to color the internal branches as well? or just color them with the same color?

THANK YOU!


## Usnea tree
Usnea.tax<-read.table("usnea.tree.tax.txt") ## taxonomy of the tree
Usnea.phylum <- read.table("usnea.phylum.txt") #file with each node taxonomy and the group:phylum
Usnea.tree<-read.nexus("usnea.tree.txt") ##Nexus tree

dd <- data.frame(taxa = Usnea.tax,
                 Phylum = Usnea.phylum)
row.names(dd) <- NULL

#usnea color
g.usnea<-ggtree(Usnea.tree, layout ="fan", aes(color=Phylum), alpha=0.8) %<+% dd
g.usnea<-g.usnea+scale_color_manual(values=c( "cadetblue3","gold2" ,"salmon4","gray45","darkorange","goldenrod","navajowhite4","khaki3","pink4","rosybrown3" ,
                               "darkolivegreen4","plum3","palevioletred", "mistyrose", "darkorange4",  "ivory2",
                               "olivedrab3", "darkcyan", "goldenrod3","indianred2"))

messages.author: 1d63b70cc6085e65
messages.subject: Re: Color internal branches error.
parts:
Hi,

I have solved your problem.  After running the command g.usnea<-ggtree(Usnea.tree, layout ="fan", aes(color=Phylum), alpha=0.8) %<+% dd
you will see that there is a dataframe layer called g.usnea$data.
If you look at the levels of g.usnea$data$Phylum, you will see 18 factor levels:

> levels(g.usnea$data$Phylum)
 [1] "Acidobacteria"         "Actinobacteria"        "Armatimonadetes"       "Bacteria_unclassified" "Bacteroidetes"         "Chlamydiae"            "Chloroflexi"          
 [8] "Cyanobacteria"         "Elusimicrobia"         "Firmicutes"            "Fusobacteria"          "Gemmatimonadetes"      "Planctomycetes"        "Proteobacteria"       
[15] "Tenericutes"           "Thermi"                "TM7"                   "Verrucomicrobia"


The 19th factor does not exist as it takes the value <NA> and so does not receive a colour.  You need to create this 19th level.  You do that like this:

levels(g.usnea$data$Phylum) <- c(levels(g.usnea$data$Phylum), 'Ancestral') #This adds a new factor level called 'Ancestral' to the factor levels in g.usnea$data$Phylum
g.usnea$data[which(is.na(g.usnea$data$Phylum)), 'Phylum'] <- 'Ancestral' #Assign the level 'Ancestral' to all those that were <NA>

Now, if you set your 19th color to 'black' (or whatever colour you choose), you can plot the tree with colors on all the branches.
